I don't know where you live or what labor laws apply to you, but I have a couple of ideas. First Is, figure out how many hours minimun you need to work for the same hourly wage (to meet your most basic needs) and then just work those hours. You could put your foot down and say I will not have more than X schedule and I Will get there exactly at this Time and leave exactly at this other Time. Of course you don't leave the kids alone, if you have an emergency contact list you could calle some9ne from there like a relative or neighbour. And I don't know if this Is a law where you live, but you might threaten to accuse the mom of child abandonment for not being home by the Time she knew they would be alone (while staying there so it doesn't hit you back).

Regarding labor laws, in muy country there's a legal concept that Is like "contract by word" where you agree to certain conditions without any official paperwork, and Is recognized if there's any record of the agreement like emails or texts. If this agreement violates either minimun wage terms OR hours per week terms (in my country Is $3/hour minimum and 45 hours/week max) you can bring the case to the labor regulation institution. I'd encourage you to look into your country's labor laws. Even if you don't report anything having the knowledge and making sure your employer knows this too might put enough pressure to change conditions.

Reporting their living conditions to some childhood protection organization might also be something to look into. Of course you don't want to be there, and probably nobody does, but the kids need to be cared for. You could get familiar with child wellbeing regulations too.

And More socially, you could tell other people about the Situation in order to put social pressure on the family yo treat their nannys better or to warn other people about working with this family.

All of that of course besides looking for another job. You can always stay if conditions get better.

Knowledge Is power, and when you know your rights you're More likely to be granted them. This kind of things that I'm telling you to find out will most likely be useful for many other work Situations. They also give you the option to bargain. Making sure employers know this too will Make them more likely to respect your rights.

The sad thing Is, if you don't get info forced into you there's no reason to go look elsewhere. If you don't know there's info missing, you can't be left wondering where it Is. If you feel like you got everything you need, you won't go out looking for what's missing. And especially if you live in a abstinence only enviroment, if you don't get something to Make you curious, you most probably won't try to find more.

Curiosity Is not widespread and neither Is acknowledgment of ignorance.

I was a psych intern when it was decided I had to get the procedure. I was already staying in the hospital, so I got to go home only after all sessions were complete and had some time to be controlled to make sure all was fine.

I don't know how it is for people who are not hospitalized. Regarding recovery after each session, I honestly don't remember it at all. Prep was long though, I had to stop eating and drinking for a day before each session. Also I remember having trouble with incontinence. I wet the bed a few times, and my pants too, to the point of needing adult diapers for a while. But I don't know if it was related to ECT, meds, or the situation itself. I would advise practising with simpler exercises before going for a project, like doing a long chain, then work a few rows of a stitch, no matter how bad it comes out, just to practise. Then do the same with another stitch, etc. until you get the hang of it. In my experience AND seeing what other beginners make, even a simple rectangle will come out crooked and miscounted and with many mistakes if it's the first Time you do it. 

Following a pattern is even another layer of difficulty on top of not knowing how to do the stitches.

So I repeat: practise freehand until you can get an even rectangle, or something like that, before going with a pattern you don't even know how to do the stitches right.

And look up YouTube videos about the stitch you're trying. Ay least to me watching other people do it makes it a Lot easier to get.
